questions.q: A school has $900$ students. The principal asks $60$ of them about lunch. How many students are in the sample?
questions.work: The sample is the group that was actually asked: $60$. The population is all $900$.

questions.q: A factory makes $5{,}000$ phones in a day. An inspector tests $200$ of them. How many phones are in the population?
questions.work: The population is the whole group the inspector wants to know about: all $5{,}000$. The $200$ tested are the sample.

questions.q: In a random sample of $40$ students, $10$ walk to school. What fraction of the sample walks? Write it in lowest terms.
questions.work: Part of the sample over the whole sample: $\frac{10}{40} = \frac{1}{4}$.

questions.q:
A librarian wants to know the favorite kind of book of all $800$ students. Which plan gives a random sample?
Plan A: ask the $30$ students in the book club.
Plan B: draw $30$ student numbers from all $800$.
questions.work: In Plan B every one of the $800$ students has the same chance of being drawn. The book club is not like the whole school.

questions.q: In a random sample of $80$ students, $30\%$ chose soccer. How many students in the sample chose soccer?
questions.work: $30\%$ of the sample: $0.30 \cdot 80 = 24$.

questions.q: A spinner landed on red $12$ times in $40$ spins. What fraction of the spins were red? Write it in lowest terms.
questions.work: Reds over all spins: $\frac{12}{40} = \frac{3}{10}$.

questions.q: A number cube was rolled $50$ times and showed a 4 on $10$ of the rolls. It will be rolled $300$ more times. Use these results to predict the number of 4s.
questions.work: The trial says $\frac{10}{50} = \frac{1}{5}$ of the rolls. Then $\frac{1}{5} \cdot 300 = 60$.

questions.q: A coin landed heads $27$ times in $60$ flips. Use these results to predict the number of heads in $400$ more flips.
questions.work: Use what happened, not what should happen: $\frac{27}{60} = \frac{9}{20}$. Then $\frac{9}{20} \cdot 400 = 180$.

questions.q: In a trial, $35\%$ of the seeds sprouted. Tomorrow $600$ seeds will be planted. Use the trial to predict the number that sprout.
A marble is drawn from a bag and put back, $80$ times. $28$ of the draws were blue. Use these results to predict how many of the next $200$ draws will NOT be blue.
questions.work: Not blue: $80 - 28 = 52$ of the $80$ draws, and $\frac{52}{80} = \frac{13}{20}$. Then $\frac{13}{20} \cdot 200 = 130$.

questions.q: In a random sample of $50$ students, $8$ ride a bike to school. The school has $600$ students. Predict how many ride a bike.
questions.work: The sample fraction times the population: $\frac{8}{50} \cdot 600 = 96$.

questions.q: In a random sample of $200$ light bulbs, $6$ are faulty. A shipment holds $3{,}000$ bulbs. Predict the number of faulty bulbs in the shipment.
questions.work: $\frac{6}{200} = \frac{3}{100}$ of the sample is faulty. Then $\frac{3}{100} \cdot 3{,}000 = 90$.

questions.q: In a random sample of $250$ voters, $40\%$ say yes. The town has $7{,}000$ voters. Predict how many of them would say yes.
questions.work: The percent goes with the population, not with the $250$: $0.40 \cdot 7{,}000 = 2{,}800$.

questions.q: $14$ students in a club are seventh graders. That is $20\%$ of the club. How many students are in the club?
questions.work: This time the whole group is missing: $20\%$ of the club is $14$, so the club is $14 \div 0.20 = 70$.

questions.q: A ranger tags $30$ turtles and lets them go. Later she catches $120$ turtles at random, and $9$ of them are tagged. Estimate the number of turtles in the pond.
questions.work: $\frac{9}{120} = \frac{3}{40}$ of the second catch is tagged, so the $30$ tagged turtles are about $\frac{3}{40}$ of the pond: $30 \div \frac{3}{40} = 400$.

questions.q: A side that is $4$ cm long is $12$ cm long in the scaled copy. Find the scale factor.
questions.work: Copy over original: $12 \div 4 = 3$.

questions.q: A triangle has a perimeter of $30$ cm. It is redrawn with a scale factor of $2.5$. Find the perimeter of the copy.
questions.work: Every side is multiplied by $2.5$, so the perimeter is too: $30 \cdot 2.5 = 75$.

questions.q: A rectangle has an area of $15\ \text{cm}^2$. It is redrawn with a scale factor of $4$. Find the area of the copy.
questions.work: Length and width are both multiplied by $4$, so the area is multiplied by $4 \cdot 4 = 16$: $15 \cdot 16 = 240$.

questions.q: A shape has a perimeter of $48$ in. It is redrawn with a scale factor of $\frac{1}{4}$. Find the new perimeter.
questions.work: A scale factor less than 1 shrinks it: $48 \cdot \frac{1}{4} = 12$.

questions.q: A figure's perimeter goes from $12$ cm to $60$ cm when it is scaled. Its original area is $8\ \text{cm}^2$. Find the area of the copy.
questions.work: The scale factor is $60 \div 12 = 5$. Area uses it twice: $8 \cdot 5 \cdot 5 = 200$.

questions.q: A plan uses the scale 1 in. : $5$ ft. A wall is $9$ in. long on the plan. How long is the real wall?
questions.work: Each inch on the plan is $5$ ft: $9 \cdot 5 = 45$.

questions.q: A map uses the scale 1 cm : $20$ km. Two towns are really $160$ km apart. How far apart are they on the map?
questions.work: Going from real to map, divide: $160 \div 20 = 8$.

questions.q: A plan uses the scale 1 cm : $5$ m. What is the scale factor from the plan to the real thing?
questions.work: Put both in the same unit first: $5$ m is $500$ cm. So 1 cm stands for $500$ cm, and the scale factor is $500$.

questions.q: A plan uses the scale 1 in. : $4$ ft. This room is $6$ in. by $5$ in. on the plan. Find the room's real area.
questions.work: Scale each side first: $6 \cdot 4 = 24$ ft and $5 \cdot 4 = 20$ ft. Then $24 \cdot 20 = 480$.

questions.q: A real garden is $30$ ft by $18$ ft. A plan of it uses the scale 1 in. : $6$ ft. Find the garden's area on the plan.
questions.work: Scale each side down first: $30 \div 6 = 5$ in. and $18 \div 6 = 3$ in. Then $5 \cdot 3 = 15$.

final.q: A plan uses the scale 1 in. : $8$ ft. On the plan, this gym floor is $10$ in. by $6$ in. Find the real area of the gym floor.
final.work: Scale each side first: $10 \cdot 8 = 80$ ft and $6 \cdot 8 = 48$ ft. Then $80 \cdot 48 = 3{,}840$. (Or: $60\ \text{in}^2$ on the plan, and each square inch is $8 \cdot 8 = 64\ \text{ft}^2$.)
